{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "ACKed after author addressed objection to SaturatingAdd and adopted suggestions to limit bantime to uint32"
    },
    {
      "login": "willcl-ark",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "pointed out bantime > uint32 in settings.json throws on startup"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:5872774469",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Supporting durations unsupported by C++ chrono using SaturatingAdd does not work for chrono types; excessively large bantime arguments should be rejected instead",
      "quote": "I am not sure about starting/trying to support durations that C++ itself doesn't even support... Also, `SaturatingAdd` doesn't work for chrono types ...",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "author switched to rejecting large bantimes and reviewer accepted with an ACK",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5874821692"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5886145451",
      "status_by_quote": "Seems fine to reject or clamp values larger than any meaningful use-case."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4130336905",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Reject relative ban times above UINT32_MAX to avoid a time dependency",
      "quote": "This should be more than enough and also avoid the weird time dependency.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "author implemented uint32 limit in setban and reviewer ACKed",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4130783968"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5886145451",
      "status_by_quote": "lgtm ACK d49c1c9ab3e139158d76141b71943ff79903e87a"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4130336905",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Parse bantime as u32",
      "quote": "What about parsing it as u32?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "author parsed -bantime as uint32_t and reviewer ACKed",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4130783968"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5886145451",
      "status_by_quote": "lgtm ACK d49c1c9ab3e139158d76141b71943ff79903e87a"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4164461680",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "A bantime value greater than uint32 in settings.json throws during conversion on startup",
      "quote": "settings.json can also have a value > uint32 which will throw during conversion",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author reverted -bantime parsing to int64, capped at UINT32_MAX, and added a test case",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4166957853"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4166957853",
      "status_by_quote": "`-bantime` is now read as int64 again and capped at UINT32_MAX, so it no longer matters where the value comes from."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:5886145451",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "Seems fine to reject or clamp values larger than any meaningful use-case.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "willcl-ark to review fix for settings.json bantime parsing",
      "id": "rc:4166957853"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "willcl-ark pointed out an issue where values > uint32 in settings.json throw on startup; the author pushed a fix parsing as int64 and capping at UINT32_MAX."
}
